title: Running on Empty
plain_title: The fiscal 2026 preliminary budget is short $3.6 billion
what_they_audited: A Citizens Budget Commission report analyzing Mayor Eric Adams' fiscal year 2026 preliminary budget for New York City.
background: The budget is balanced on paper, and the city has been covering recent shortfalls with surplus funds it accumulated through fiscal year 2022.

findings.plain: The preliminary budget does not include enough money to pay for the services the city plans to provide.
findings.quote: The fiscal year 2026 preliminary budget is short $3.6 billion needed to provide planned services

findings.plain: In each of the two prior fiscal years the city's expenses ran ahead of its revenues.
findings.quote: Expenses exceeded revenues by $636.0 million in fiscal year 2023 and $1.1 billion in fiscal year 2024, adjusted for the City’s ability to shift timing of payments

findings.plain: The surplus the city rolls from year to year has been shrinking.
findings.quote: declined from $6.1 billion in fiscal year 2022 to $4.4 billion in fiscal year 2024

findings.plain: The practice of budgeting less than programs actually cost has grown.
findings.quote: the City’s habit of underbudgeting current services has grown substantially, exceeding $4.0 billion a year

findings.plain: During fiscal year 2025 the city had to add billions mid-year for programs the group had flagged as underbudgeted.
findings.quote: The City has already added $3.8 billion during fiscal year 2025 to fund programs that CBC identified as underbudgeted at the beginning of the fiscal year

findings.plain: Future gaps are far larger once underbudgeting, the class size mandate and asylum seeker costs are counted.
findings.quote: Future budget gaps are $7.8 billion, $10.1 billion, and $9.6 billion in fiscal years 2027 to 2029, respectively

numbers.label: Shortfall in the fiscal 2026 preliminary budget
Added mid-year in fiscal 2025 for underbudgeted programs
Addition to the general reserve the report proposes

recommendations: Present accurate, reasonable estimates of expenses and revenue in the fiscal year 2026 executive budget, as the City Charter requires.
Run a Program to Eliminate the Gap that streamlines administrative operations, raises program efficiency and scales back or ends the programs delivering the least value to residents.
Do not fund new or expanded programs in the executive budget or at adoption.
Add at least $1.0 billion to the fiscal year 2026 general reserve to help respond to potential federal cuts.
